title: Race conditions, deadlocks and priority inversion
summary: The three classic concurrency bugs: two threads changing the same data (race), two threads waiting on each other forever (deadlock), and important work stuck behind unimportant work (priority inversion).
body: **Race condition:** the result depends on timing. Example: two threads do `count += 1` at once; both read 5, both write 6 - one increment is lost. Fix: protect shared state with an actor, a serial queue or a `Mutex`, or avoid shared mutable state with value types.

**Deadlock:** A waits for B while B waits for A, so both wait forever. iOS examples: `DispatchQueue.main.sync` from the main thread; two locks taken in opposite order by two threads; a semaphore waiting for work that needs the same blocked thread. Fix: never `sync` onto your own queue, always take locks in the same order, avoid blocking waits in async code.

**Priority inversion:** a high-priority task (UI) waits for a lock held by a low-priority task, which barely gets CPU time, so the UI hangs. Fix: use locks that support priority donation (`Mutex`, `os_unfair_lock`), avoid semaphores between QoS levels, and do not make the main thread wait on background work.
**Livelock / starvation:** threads keep reacting to each other without progress, or a task never gets a turn. Rare on iOS but good to name.

**Tools:** Thread Sanitizer (TSan) catches data races at runtime; Main Thread Checker catches UI calls off main; Swift 6 strict concurrency catches many races at compile time; Instruments shows blocked threads.
keyPoints: Race: unsynchronized shared mutable state - fix with actors, serial queues, `Mutex` or value types.
Deadlock: circular waiting - classic is `main.sync` on main.
Priority inversion: high priority blocked by low priority holding a resource.
Swift 6 catches data races at compile time; TSan catches them at runtime.
Actors remove data races but not logical race conditions (reentrancy).

mistakes: Saying "it worked when I tested it" - races depend on timing and appear in production.
Using a semaphore to make async code synchronous.
followups: **How would you debug a crash that happens 1 in 1,000 runs?** Enable TSan, run tests repeatedly, look for shared mutable state, check crash logs for multiple threads in the same code.
**Are actors enough to avoid all concurrency bugs?** No - they prevent data races but you can still have ordering bugs across `await`.
